name: The Ritz-Carlton, Amelia Island
insider_take: This oceanfront sanctuary sits on Florida's northernmost barrier island, where wild horses once roamed and pirates once hid treasure along 13 miles of pristine beaches.
whats_special: The Ritz-Carlton Amelia Island occupies a rare slice of untouched Atlantic coastline where sea turtles nest annually from May through October. The resort's championship golf course was designed by Pete Dye and features dramatic ocean views from 8 holes. Historic Fernandina Beach, just minutes away, boasts one of Florida's largest collections of Victorian architecture with over 50 buildings on the National Register of Historic Places.
pro_tip: Book a turtle walk experience during nesting season (May-August) to witness loggerhead sea turtles laying eggs on the beach - it's a magical experience available nowhere else in Northeast Florida.
dont_miss: Explore Fort Clinch State Park's Civil War fort and pristine beaches, take a sunset horseback ride along the shore, or stroll Fernandina's historic Centre Street district for antique shopping and local seafood at centuries-old establishments like the Palace Saloon - Florida's oldest continuously operating bar since 1878.
pros: Pristine oceanfront location with direct beach access
Legendary Ritz-Carlton service and luxury amenities
Championship golf course and world-class spa facilities
Historic Amelia Island charm with nature preserve surroundings
cons: Premium pricing reflective of luxury brand positioning
Remote island location requiring longer travel times
